known_facts_book1: An old Witch who used to live in the Gillikin Country, north of Dr. Pipt's mountain.
Was given all of Dr. Pipt's first Powder of Life and cheated him wickedly in return, paying with a Powder of Perpetual Youth that was no good and could work no magic at all.
Used that Powder of Life to bring Jack Pumpkinhead to life, to test it.
Stole Ozma as a baby and transformed her into a boy, and made her carry wood and hoe the garden.
Appears nowhere in this book: she exists only in Margolotte's and Ozma's accounts of things long past.

known_relations_book1.Dr. Pipt: Cheated him out of his first Powder of Life.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: Stole and transformed her as a baby, and was fled from.
known_relations_book1.Jack Pumpkinhead: Brought him to life with the stolen powder.

known_facts_book1: Described in this book only as 'an ordinary young lady named Jinjur', an old friend of the Scarecrow.
Repaints the Scarecrow's faded left ear for him, which restores his hearing on that side.
Always fixes the Scarecrow up when he gets weather-worn.
Never appears on the page: the Scarecrow rides off to visit her and comes back with the ear freshly painted.

Has hatched about seven thousand chicks in all, by the Soldier's reckoning.
Is named in the Shaggy Man's song as 'one wise Yellow Hen'.
Never appears on the page in this book; she is only reported and sung about.

known_facts_book1: Dorothy's kitten, all pink — brains and all — except for blue eyes, and a great favorite at the royal palace.
Is an ordinary kitten, not made of glass, which the Glass Cat finds hard to credit.
Is the subject of the Shaggy Man's advice to Bungle: make friends with the Pink Kitten and you will be solid at the palace.
Never appears on the page in this book; she is only talked about.

known_facts_book1: The Highly Magnified professor of the Royal College of Athletics.
Invented the Square Meal Tablets that the Shaggy Man carries, each containing soup, fish, roast meat, salad, apple-dumplings, ice cream and chocolate-drops boiled down to a fingernail-sized tablet.
Is named in the Shaggy Man's song as one who looks so big to everyone that he is filled with pride.
Never appears on the page in this book.

known_facts_book1: One of the two enormous beasts that crouch at Ozma's feet and guard her when she holds high court in the Throne Room.
Is well known and respected in the Emerald City, and is a friend and playmate of Toto.
Is named in the Shaggy Man's song as the beast who shakes with fear almost every time he roars, and yet does the bravest things.
Stands behind Ozma with the Hungry Tiger at the final scene when the statues are restored.
Speaks no line in this book and takes no part in the plot.
